metadata.title: Push The One File.
metadata.subtitle: Cardputer Buddy — Claude Code Plugin (Dev-Loop Scripts)
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: after a Cardputer app is already installed, does changing one file mean reinstalling the whole app directory, or is there a script built for exactly a single-file push? Lands the carry-out that push.py and install_apps.py can both do the job, but only one matches the size of a one-file change.

beats.narration_text: Someone assumed a one-file change meant reinstalling everything on the device. It doesn't — there's a script for exactly that. So: I changed one file on my Cardputer — do I push it?

beats.narration_text: The Cardputer runs MicroPython on a slash-flash filesystem. main-dot-py is the launcher — it scans the apps folder at boot and lists every dot-py file it finds as a menu entry, automatically. Drop a new file into that folder, push it to the device, and it shows up on the next boot — no registration code needed anywhere. The payload has three zones: the launcher itself, a shared library of BLE, UI, state, and protocol code, and the apps folder holding whatever's installed. When you're writing a new app, you start from hello_cardputer-dot-py — the smallest working example, covering keyboard polling, font rendering, and the convention for exiting back to the launcher.

production_viz.label: /FLASH/ · LAUNCHER · TEMPLATE
production_viz.caption: drop a .py in apps/ — no registration

beats.narration_text: Four scripts drive everyday changes. install_apps-dot-py pushes the entire apps folder over USB-serial — reach for it when you've added or renamed files and need the whole directory back in sync. push-dot-py pushes just the files you name — reach for it when you've edited one existing file and want the fast loop. tail_serial-dot-py streams the device's serial logs — run it in a second terminal while you test. repl_run-dot-py runs a single Python expression over the REPL — handy for a quick filesystem check without pushing anything. All four need PORT, and that's whatever the provisioning step detected earlier — something like slash-dev-cu-dot-usbmodem on a Mac, slash-dev-tty-ACM on Linux, or COM on Windows.

Here's the actual overlap: install_apps-dot-py and push-dot-py can both push your one changed file. install_apps-dot-py syncs the complete apps folder every time, which takes longer than it needs to for a single edit. push-dot-py, given just that one filename, does the same job in a fraction of the time. Nothing in either script's name tells you which is faster for the change in front of you — that's a distinction you have to remember, the tools don't remind you of it.

production_viz.label: THE OVERLAP THAT BITES
production_viz.caption: both push it — only one is fast

beats.narration_text: When you've changed one file, push.py sends just that file — install_apps.py resyncs everything, whether it changed or not. Match the script to the size of the change, not habit.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: Add a timer app to the Cardputer that counts down from 60 seconds and returns to the launcher when done. Watch four things. Does it create the new file in buddy/device/apps/, following the hello_cardputer.py structure? Does it use push.py for the single new file rather than install_apps.py for the full directory? Does it follow the exit convention — polling the keyboard for a key back to the launcher — instead of hard-looping with no way out? And after pushing, does it suggest tail_serial.py to watch the output, instead of asking you to re-flash?
